subject.title: memory-lancedb: stale recall can answer 'latest' queries without recency/provenance

question: Should memory-lancedb solve freshness-sensitive recall locally now, wait for the broader tool freshness metadata contract, or combine a narrow plugin fix with a later shared provenance API?
rationale: The source bug is concrete, but the durable product boundary affects memory ranking semantics, assistant-visible provenance, and overlap with the open shared freshness-metadata RFC.

options.title: Land a narrow plugin fix first
options.body: Refresh the linked PR or a replacement so memory-lancedb uses createdAt/source timestamps for freshness-sensitive recall and includes provenance hints, then leave broader metadata standardization to the RFC.

options.title: Block on the shared freshness contract
options.body: Keep this issue open but defer implementation until maintainers define the shared tool-response freshness/provenance envelope in the RFC.

options.title: Close as RFC-owned
options.body: Treat the stale recall symptom as fully owned by the broader freshness metadata RFC, accepting that memory-lancedb remains unresolved until that larger design lands.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow plugin fix first
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR or a replacement so memory-lancedb uses createdAt/source timestamps for freshness-sensitive recall and includes provenance hints, then leave broader metadata standardization to the RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest memory-lancedb history signal and is best placed to choose whether the fix belongs in the plugin now or a broader shared API later.
